summary:
LUNAR NAVIGATOR is an interactive web-based decision-support tool designed to help users explore and compare potential lunar landing sites near the Moon's south pole.

Using NASA data and scientific resources, the platform analyzes solar illumination, Earth visibility for communication, and surrounding terrain conditions to evaluate the operational suitability of different landing locations.

Unlike conventional lunar maps, LUNAR NAVIGATOR brings multiple mission-critical factors together in one intuitive interface. Users can compare predefined candidate sites, explore the relationship between landing location and mission timing, and enter custom coordinates to investigate their own locations.

By transforming complex astronomical and topographical calculations into accessible visualizations, our project aims to make lunar exploration data easier to understand and support more informed decisions about where and when future lunar missions should land.
details:
Project Overview

LUNAR NAVIGATOR is an interactive lunar landing site exploration and comparison platform focused on the Moon's south polar region.

The lunar south pole is a strategically important region for future exploration because of its potential water ice resources and unique environmental conditions. However, its extreme terrain and illumination patterns create significant challenges for landing operations. Some areas experience prolonged darkness, while others receive sunlight for extended periods. Communication with Earth can also be restricted by the surrounding terrain.

Our project addresses these challenges by combining multiple scientific factors into a single accessible interface.

Core Features

1. Solar Illumination Analysis

The platform calculates when and for how long a selected location receives sunlight.

This helps users understand potential solar power availability and identify favorable landing periods.

2. Earth Visibility and Communication Analysis

LUNAR NAVIGATOR evaluates whether Earth is visible from a selected landing location.

By considering terrain obstructions, the platform helps users identify potential communication windows and periods of signal interruption.

3. Terrain and Horizon Analysis

Using lunar elevation data, the system analyzes surrounding terrain and local horizon conditions.

This provides additional context for understanding illumination and communication constraints that cannot be explained by geographic coordinates alone.

4. Candidate Site Comparison

Users can explore six predefined lunar south pole candidate locations, alongside two reference locations: Chandrayaan-3 and Apollo 11.

They can compare environmental conditions across locations and investigate how different landing sites affect mission operations.

5. Custom Coordinate Exploration

Users can enter their own coordinates and explore environmental conditions at locations beyond the predefined candidates.

This makes the platform useful not only for comparing known sites but also for independent exploration and investigation.

Technical Implementation

The project combines several technologies:

  • Frontend: Vite, React 19, TypeScript
  • Visualization: WebGL-based interactive 3D Moon
  • Backend: Java 26, Spring Boot 4
  • Scientific Computation: Python 3.11+
  • Astronomical Calculations: NASA Horizons
  • Terrain Analysis: Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) elevation data

NASA Horizons is used to obtain astronomical information for calculating the positions of relevant celestial bodies. LOLA elevation data supports terrain and horizon analysis.

The system also uses precomputed scientific results and backend caching to make complex calculations more accessible and efficient.

Innovation and Impact

The main innovation of LUNAR NAVIGATOR is its integration of multiple mission-critical environmental factors into one interactive exploration experience.

Instead of requiring users to navigate separate scientific tools and interpret complex datasets independently, our platform presents solar illumination, Earth visibility, and terrain conditions together.

We aim to bridge the gap between scientific data and practical exploration by making lunar landing site analysis understandable to a broader audience, including students, educators, and people interested in space exploration.

Ultimately, LUNAR NAVIGATOR seeks to help users answer two fundamental questions:

Where should a lunar mission land, and when is the best time to do so?
